Status (sketch, built, verified, approved) lives only in `screen-status.yaml`.
States come from the five-state vocabulary: empty, typical, overflow, error, loading.

the others use the pairwise set (U252).

## shell

| Screen | Id | Units | Platforms | States | Variants | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| App shell | `shell.root` | U150 | iphone, ipad, mac | typical, loading, error | pairwise set | `sidebar`, `tab-bar`, `toolbar` |
| Keyboard shortcuts help | `shell.keyboardShortcuts` | U158 | ipad, mac | typical, overflow | pairwise set | `sheet-form` |
| Damaged collection | `shell.damagedCollection` | U153, U163a, U251 | iphone, ipad, mac | empty, typical, error, loading | pairwise set | `content-unavailable`, `confirmation-dialog` |

- `shell.root`: Root layout with the sidebar on iPad and Mac and the tab bar on iPhone, plus the status overlay.
- `shell.keyboardShortcuts`: The list of keyboard shortcuts for the current context.
- `shell.damagedCollection`: Shown in Failed{Corrupt} (engine/lifecycle L1, maintenance/optimize-integrity M7) in place of the whole root content: no sidebar, tab bar, deck list or review. A native content-unavailable view with the exclamationmark.triangle symbol, the title "This Collection Is Damaged" and one line, "Meguri stopped saving changes and sending anything to iCloud so the damage can't spread.", then the remedies as buttons in M7.1's order, each shown only while M7.1 offers it: "Check Database" (U163 once U128 lands), "Restore from Backup…" (when the backups listing holds a backup or server copy; opens settings.backups' restore sheet with the newest restorable backup preselected) and "Replace with iCloud Collection…" (only when sync/cloudkit-recovery V19's conditions hold; opens its V14 preview). The first offered remedy has the prominent style, the others the bordered style; "Copy Debug Info" is always there as a plain button below them. No remedy downloads from an Anki server. Empty: no remedy is offered, so the line adds "No backup or iCloud copy of this collection is available on this device." and only Copy Debug Info shows. Loading: Check Database's stages or the iCloud entry's progress replace the buttons, with Cancel while the operation says stopping is safe. Error: Check Database or the iCloud entry failing or refusing (Check Database's corrupt verdict, offline, SafetyBackupFailed) shows its reason in one line above the remaining buttons; the screen stays. A restore started here reports its progress and errors in settings.backups' restore sheet. A remedy that succeeds returns to the deck workspace. Every menu command that needs a collection is disabled; Settings, Copy Debug Info and Quit stay available. In Settings every row stored in the collection is disabled; device-local rows, Backups' Restore from Backup… and Show in Finder or Files, and About stay usable.

- `home.deckList`: The deck tree as a native list (native-interface-contract N2, N11.5): each row the deck's last name component with the non-zero New, Learning and To Review counts as secondary text, the Mac and iPad sidebar rows with a To Review badge; then the activity section (studied-today line, heatmap, streak stats; U228) in the same list on every layout; and the sync button.
- `home.deckPage`: One deck's labelled New, Learning and To Review counts with the buried "+N" badge (U228a), the Study button, the finished state, and the deck-scoped heatmap, streak stats and Stats action (U228).
- `home.deckMenu`: One menu for a deck, shown as the row's context menu (right-click, long press) and the Mac row's hover ⋯ button, in R47's order with Delete separated and destructive and Unbury only with buried cards; a filtered deck's menu offers only Rename and Delete (R53). On iPhone a row swipe shows Options and More, never Delete (R49). The menu bar's Deck menu is U159's and follows R283. Until U156 lands the menu holds Study and Overview (U152). Delete of a subtree with cards asks first with the deck and card counts (confirmation-dialog); deletes and moves end with an Undo toast.
- `home.deckName`: The sheet for Create Deck, New Subdeck (prefilled "<parent>::", cursor at the end) and Rename (prefilled full path): one name field, Cancel and a confirm button disabled for an empty or blank name. Error: the refused move or name in one line under the field; a final name that differs from the typed one is reported after saving.
- `home.goToDeck`: Filter decks by name and jump to one.
- `home.sessionSummary`: A sheet over the restored deck workspace (window sheet on Mac, form sheet on iPad, sheet on iPhone), shown when R91 says (queue empty, timebox Finish, Back to Decks or Esc after at least one answer). Title "Session Summary"; toolbar Done (confirmation action; Return and Esc too) and Undo (⌘Z; while an answer can be undone). A grouped list: (1) totals: cards studied and time ("42 cards in 12 minutes"), Again, Hard, Good and Easy counts as four labelled values, "Passed" as the percentage of answers that were not Again, and new cards introduced; (2) What's Next: remaining today with a bordered Continue button after an early close (Done keeps Return), or the time until the next learning card, or "Finished for today" with tomorrow's due count; the finished state's limit and buried notes with their actions (R94); (3) the streak line once U228 fills its slot, taking no space before; (4) Missed Cards in first-miss order: question excerpt (two lines at most), deck name as secondary text, the miss count trailing ("2×"), a deleted card labelled "Deleted card"; a row opens the read-only preview once U186 attaches it, and "Browse Missed Cards" sits under the section once U210 attaches it. Empty: no missed cards, the section reads "No missed cards". Overflow: many missed cards scroll inside the sheet; the toolbar stays. The deck page's "Last Session" opens the same sheet read-only: title "Last Session", no Undo, Continue or Unbury. No chart.
- `home.fsrsSheet`: The FSRS-only notice and parameter optimization status for a collection.

- `review.question`: The card's question side in quiet corners (native-interface-contract N3, N11.1, N11.2): Back to Decks at the upper left, the timer, touch undo and ⋯ and the sync status icon at the upper right, the thin progress bar under them, the card scrolling between them and a reserved bottom action region holding the Show Answer button.
- `review.answer`: The answer side: the same corners and card position as the question side, and in the same bottom region the Again, Hard, Good and Easy buttons in one row, interval as the prominent label and grade name secondary, no key hints (N11.2). iPhone (compact width, any iPad window that narrow): full screen above the hidden tab bar with the status bar visible, the exit an xmark close button named "Back to Decks", undo and ⋯ at the upper right, the bottom region above the home indicator and clear of the fold, buttons at least 44 pt tall with Dynamic Type capped to keep one row (R358), card taps and tap zones as U180. iPad at regular width: the review fills the window with the sidebar hidden for the whole session, the labelled Back to Decks button, and the iPhone touch rules; with a hardware keyboard the shortcuts appear in the menu bar and the ⌘ overlay, not on the buttons. - `review.setDueDate`: Set the current card's due date from the review screen.
- `review.forget`: Reset the current card to new with its two remembered options.
- `review.editCurrent`: Edit the note of the card under review without leaving the session.
- `review.congratulations`: Nothing left to study today, with what comes next.

## editor

| Screen | Id | Units | Platforms | States | Variants | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Add note (signature) | `editor.add` | U190, U192, U193, U195 | iphone, ipad, mac | empty, typical, overflow, error | full covering set | `editor`, `toolbar`, `sheet-form`, `toast`, `confirmation-dialog` |
| Edit note | `editor.edit` | U190, U196 | iphone, ipad, mac | typical, overflow, error | pairwise set | `editor`, `inspector` |

- `editor.add`: Add notes (U195). Entry points (R796, notes/add-defaults D3): the Home toolbar "+", the review ⋯ menu, Browse's Add Notes and the A key; from a deck, with that deck preset (D1 preset_deck): the deck page "+", the deck menu's Add Note, the empty deck page and Browse's sidebar; Create Copy (Browse, review ⋯) and AnkiConnect guiAddCards. Mac: a resizable trailing panel in the main window beside the current content, never a separate window; iPad: a page sheet; iPhone: a sheet at full height (large detent; decided 2026-10-27: this is R796's and U195's "full-screen sheet", kept a sheet so that the swipe-down reaches R816's prompt). The draft is kept above the layout, so it survives size changes (R5). Layout, top to bottom, one form: the Type and Deck rows (R797), each showing the current name; on Mac each opens a popover with a searchable list, on iPad and iPhone each pushes a searchable list inside the sheet; the deck list leaves out filtered decks and an empty Default deck with no subdecks. Then the fields in order (U190), each labelled with its name and with a pin toggle for its sticky option (R805); the formatting controls (U192: a toolbar row above the fields on Mac, the keyboard accessory on iPad and iPhone); the Tags field with suggestions (U193; tags/complete C5: at most 500, "::" shown as "∷"). Mac panel: a header with the title "Add Note" and a close button, and a bottom bar with History and the prominent Add button. Sheets: a close button (system close role) at the leading edge, History and the prominent Add button (confirmation action) at the trailing edge. Image occlusion note types hand the field area to U206. Defaults: on open, and on a reopen while the draft is blank, the screen asks notes/add-defaults D1 with the card under review and the entry's deck (D3, D4); a draft that is not blank is kept unchanged. A note type change maps the content (R802) and, with addToCur off, selects D2's deck when it gives one (editor/config-keys K4.2). After each change set the screen checks its selection (D5). Create Copy and a prefilled draft replace an unchanged draft, or ask first (D3). Live check (notes/field-check K1): 600 ms after a change and when a field loses focus. Duplicate: the first field is marked and the line "A note with this first field already exists." shows with a "Show Duplicates" button, which opens Browse on the dupe: search built by search/join-and-replace J3, or on nid: with the found notes when J3.4 refuses the text; a duplicate never blocks adding (R808). Each cloze state shows its line under the fields (R812); the empty state shows its line only once some field is not empty (decided 2026-10-27: a blank draft shows no line, which narrows notes/field-check K5's live hint for that draft, and a refusal names its cause in place, with no alert). Line texts are Meguri's own (String Catalog). Add (⌘↩, R813): flushes the editor and runs the check again; empty, notetype_not_cloze and field_not_cloze refuse (R809, R810): no alert, the state's line shows (on a blank draft the empty line appears now) and stays, focus moves to the first field and VoiceOver announces the line; missing_cloze asks first (confirmation-dialog "Add without a cloze deletion?", Add and Cancel; R811); otherwise the note is added with update_add_defaults true (D6), as one undo step "Add Note" (R814), and a toast says "1 card added" or "N cards added" with Undo. The next draft keeps the sticky fields and every tag, and focus returns to the first field (D6). History (⇧⌘H, R815): a popover (Mac, iPad) or a pushed list (iPhone) of the notes added since launch, newest first, each the first 30 characters of its first field; a row opens Browse on nid:<id>; a deleted note's row is disabled as "(Note deleted)"; with no notes it says "No notes added yet." Close (R816, R259): Esc, ⌘W, the close button and the iPhone swipe-down; when the draft is not unchanged since the last add (D4), confirmation-dialog "Discard current input?" with Discard (destructive) and Keep Editing. Empty: a blank draft of the default note type and deck, no lines, Add enabled. Overflow: 31 fields and long field text scroll between the Type and Deck rows and the bottom controls, which stay visible. Error: the refusals above; D1's InvalidArgument (no note type) or NotFound shows a content-unavailable view in place of the form, with Add disabled; an add that fails shows its message in one line above Add and keeps the draft; in the exclusive phase Add is disabled with "Waiting for <operation>" (KTD17), and a collection replacement asks the close prompt first. Keyboard (menu commands too): ⌘↩ Add, ⌘N Type, ⌘D Deck, ⇧⌘H History, F9 or ⌥⌘P pin the focused field, ⇧F9 pin all fields or clear all when any is pinned (R862), Esc or ⌘W close, Tab between fields. VoiceOver: each field editor is labelled with its field name; the pin is a toggle "Pin <field name>"; Type and Deck read their label and value; a line that appears after Add and the toast are announced. Core: notes/add-defaults D1 and D2, notes/field-check K1, tags/complete C1, the add op with update_add_defaults (notes/note-records A4), the sticky field update (U29), editor/config-keys K4 (addToCur is read here and set in Settings › Editing), and search/join-and-replace build for dupe: and nid:.
- `editor.edit`: Edit an existing note from the browser or review.

## browse

| Screen | Id | Units | Platforms | States | Variants | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Browser (signature) | `browse.browser` | U210, U211, U212, U213, U214, U215, U216, U218, U221, U223 | iphone, ipad, mac | empty, typical, overflow, error, loading | full covering set | `table`, `search-tokens`, `sidebar`, `inspector`, `content-unavailable` |
| Find and Replace | `browse.findReplace` | U220 | iphone, ipad, mac | typical, error | pairwise set | `sheet-form` |
| Edit Field | `browse.editField` | U220 | iphone, ipad, mac | typical, error | pairwise set | `sheet-form` |

- `browse.browser`: Search, sort and act on the collection's cards or notes (U210). Entry points: the Browse sidebar section (Mac, iPad) or tab (iPhone); ⌘F from Home, the deck page or review, with the field focused (R216); and with a given search (R1114): the deck menu's Browse, the session summary's Browse Missed Cards, Stats' Show in Browser and the heatmap, the editor's Show Duplicates, the Add history, meguri://browse?search=, Migaku and AnkiConnect. A given search gets search/join-and-replace J2's rule, is put in canonical form and runs as committed (R1109); Stats' text is the exception and shows exactly as stats/browse-queries Q3 writes it. A plain open runs defaultSearchText when it is set (browser/config-keys K6.4), otherwise deck:current with an empty field and the placeholder "Search current deck" (R1112); the placeholder reads "Search" whenever another search is the committed one. Committing an empty field (Return, live search) runs the empty search, the whole collection (search/query-model Q2), as Anki does and as search/join-and-replace J6 and J7 read it; only the open uses deck:current. From review the card under review becomes the current row and scrolls into view, or the search becomes cid:<id> when the default search does not hold it (R1113, browser/result-sets H12 index_of). Mac (R1232): the Browse section's detail holds the filter column (U216: a source list with Saved Searches, Today, Flags, Card State, Decks, Note Types and Tags, each collapsible, R1157), the table (U211) and the inspector (U221: Editor, Preview and Card Info tabs; trailing, or below the table by the device setting, R1222). The toolbar holds the search field (U214; suggestions U215), the Cards/Notes segmented picker (R1115) and the inspector toggle; ⌃⌘S shows or hides the filter column. A narrower window collapses the inspector first, then the filter column; nothing opens another window. iPad at regular width (R1233): the same columns, with the toolbar in the navigation bar; below the table's minimum width (U211 spike B1) it switches live to the compact layout and keeps search, selection and scroll position. iPhone and compact width (U223): a list with the search field pinned at the top, the quick-filter chips, two-line rows and the toolbar's Cards/Notes, Sort, Display, Select and Filters (the filter sections in a sheet); a row pushes the note detail. Table: the columns of activeCols or activeNoteCols (K4) with browser/columns C2's labels, alignment and elision; a header click sorts by that column in its first direction (browser/sorting S1) and a second click reverses it (K5.2); Question and Answer show no sort affordance; the header's context menu shows, hides and reorders columns (K4.2, K4.3); widths and row density stay on the device (K11). Rows show the flag, marked, suspended and buried tints and glyphs (C4, C5); a damaged row (C3.1) is shown disabled. The current row is separate from the selection (U212). Below the table (Mac, iPad) a status bar in the footnote style, as Finder's, reads "1,204 cards" or "3 of 1,204 cards selected", "notes" in notes mode (R1111); on iPhone the same text is the navigation subtitle. Cards/Notes writes browserTableShowNotesMode (K6.1), runs the other mode with its own columns and sort, and maps the selection and current row (H11, H12). Loading: while a search runs the previous results stay; with none, the table area shows an indeterminate progress indicator; a streamed search shows "Searching…" and the count so far in the status bar until it completes; rows not fetched yet show fixed-height placeholders (U211). Empty: a valid search with no results shows a content-unavailable view "No cards match" ("No notes match") with "Clear Search", which restores the default search (R1110). Error: an incomplete term at the cursor keeps the last valid results with no message (R1107); a syntax error underlines its range in the field, shows its message in one line at the top of the table area (under the field on iPhone; decided 2026-10-27: on Mac and iPad the field is in the toolbar, so the line under the toolbar replaces R1108's and U214's "under the field") and dims the previous results under "Results unchanged until the search is valid" (R1108, search/errors E7); a search that fails otherwise (storage, collection unavailable) shows a content-unavailable view with its message and Try Again. Changes from elsewhere refresh the visible rows in place and show a "Results changed" bar with Refresh above the table, which runs the committed search again (R1792). Overflow: 150,000 rows scroll at display rate; a truncated cell shows its full value as help text on hover (Mac) or by long press (iPad). In the exclusive phase searches still run and every mutating command is disabled (U153); CollectionReplaced returns to Home. Keyboard (menu commands, U218; R1225, R1229, R261, R272, R273): ⌘F focuses the search field and selects its text, ⇧⌘F the filter column's filter field, ⇧⌘L the table, ⌥⌘L the editor, ⌥⌘I Card Info, ⇧⌘P Preview; ↑, ↓, Home, End and ⌃⌘↑ or ⌃⌘↓ move the current row, Shift extends the selection; ⌘A in the table and ⌥⌘A elsewhere select all, ⌥⌘S inverts, ⌘C copies the selected rows; Return in the field commits. VoiceOver (R1240): a row is one element that reads its visible column values and states, with custom actions; a header reads its column and sort direction; a committed search announces its result count once; every chip, token, sidebar item and toolbar item has a label. Identifiers browse.<element>, rows browse.table.row.<id>. Core: one search session per Browse instance (browser/result-sets H2): start_search, rows, qa_cells only while Question or Answer shows (H7), reverse for a second header click and resort for a new column on a complete result, a new start_search while a search still runs (H8), toggle and map_selection (H11, H12), invalidated_rows with every change set (H10), resolve_selection for every action (H12); search/join-and-replace build, join and replace for sidebar items and chips; the reads and writes of browser/config-keys K4 to K7, each written only when the value changes (K10.1); reads never write (K2, R1138).
- `browse.findReplace`: Find and replace text in the selected notes' fields.
- `browse.editField`: Set one field across the selected notes.

## cardInfo

| Screen | Id | Units | Platforms | States | Variants | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Card Info | `cardInfo.card` | U222 | iphone, ipad, mac | empty, typical, overflow, error, loading | pairwise set | `inspector`, `charts`, `table`, `content-unavailable`, `toast` |

- `cardInfo.card`: One card's properties, review history and forgetting curve (U222, stats/card-info), read only: opening or refreshing it never writes (C1, R1252). Hosts, never a separate window (R1247, R1422): the Card Info tab of Browse's inspector (Mac, iPad; ⌥⌘I), which follows the current row live, a notes-mode row showing its note's card with the lowest template ordinal, then the lowest card id, as Anki does (decided 2026-10-27; browser/columns C1's first card, by id, is only for column values); the Card Info item of the iPhone note detail (U223); the editor's ⋯ menu and the review ⋯ menu (Card Info, Previous Card Info; on Mac also I for Card Info and ⌥⌘I for Previous Card Info during review, R1262, R1422), as a sheet: a window sheet with Done on Mac, a form sheet on iPad, a sheet with medium and large detents on iPhone; and the session summary's missed-card preview (U157). Opened from review, the sheet starts with a segmented Current/Previous picker (R1263), on Current from Card Info or I and on Previous from Previous Card Info or ⌥⌘I; Previous is disabled before the session's first answer and after every answer is undone (C9). Layout, one scrolling grouped list: (1) the stats rows of C4.1 in the core's order, the label leading and the value trailing, values exactly as the core writes them and selectable; never an Ease row (R1250); labels from the String Catalog (C12). (2) Forgetting Curve (C7), only when the snapshot has a curve (C7.1): a Swift Charts line, the past solid and the future dashed, a today marker, and the dashed Desired Retention line when it is above the chart's lower bound (C7.5); a segmented range picker (First Week, First Month, First Year, All Time) only when more than one range is offered, starting on the last one (C7.3); the tooltip of C7.6 on hover (Mac) or touch. The section is a disclosure; collapsing it is R1258's hide, saved on the device. (3) Review History (C6), newest first: a table on Mac and at regular width (Date, with the time when wide; Type in its state colour; Rating, Again in the Learn colour; Interval; Ease; Time; Stability when turned on), two-line rows at compact width; the section header's menu holds "Show Stability", saved on the device (R1254). (4) "Copy Debug Info", a bordered button that puts C8's JSON on the pasteboard and confirms with the toast "Copied to clipboard". Empty: a new card shows its rows only, with no curve and no history section. Loading: it opens within 100 ms (R1841); until the first snapshot arrives the rows are blank placeholders of their final size; a refresh replaces the content in place, keeping the range, the disclosure and the scroll position. Error: a card that does not exist, and Browse with no current row, show a content-unavailable view with C12's "(No card to display.)"; a missing or damaged record (C11) shows a content-unavailable view that names it and says Check Database can repair it. Overflow: 500 history entries scroll; long deck, note type and custom data values wrap. Live (C10, R1260): it fetches again on CardStatsChanged for the shown card and on the day change; in Browse it changes card with the current row. Keyboard: Tab reaches the picker, the range picker, the disclosure, the history menu and Copy Debug Info; Esc closes a sheet; ⌥⌘I shows or hides Browse's tab. VoiceOver: each stats row is one element ("Due, 2026-11-02"); each history entry is one element that reads its column labels and values; the chart has a summary and an audio graph; the picker is labelled "Card". Identifiers cardInfo.row.<key>, cardInfo.history, cardInfo.curve.range, cardInfo.copyDebug, cardInfo.switch. Core: the C1 snapshot through U103's export (query lane; the interactive lane from review), card_info_debug_json (C8), card_info_affected for CardStatsChanged (C10); the previous card's id comes from U175's session record (C9).

| Screen | Id | Units | Platforms | States | Variants | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Statistics (signature) | `stats.overview` | U225, U226, U230, U231 | iphone, ipad, mac | empty, typical, overflow, error, loading | full covering set | `charts`, `calendar-grid`, `toolbar`, `content-unavailable` |
| Heatmap settings | `stats.heatmapSettings` | U229 | iphone, ipad, mac | typical | pairwise set | `grouped-form`, `calendar-grid` |

- `stats.overview`: The scope and history header and the graph cards in R1357's order (Today, Future Due, Calendar, ... Added) for a deck, the collection or a search. The heatmap and streak stats are not here: they live on Home and the deck page (home.deckList, home.deckPage). The shell is U225's; the graphs are U226's, U230's and U231's (stats/graph-presentation). Entry points (R1349): the Stats sidebar section (Mac, iPad), the Stats tab (iPhone), the deck page's and the deck menu's Stats (that deck's scope) and the T key on Home and the deck page. Stats reopens with the device's last scope, deck, search and history, except when opened from a deck (R1354). Header, in the toolbar (native-interface-contract N11.7): at regular width the scope picker (Deck, Collection, Search), then the deck pop-up button listing every deck, filtered decks included (Deck scope), or a search field run on Return or when it loses focus (Search scope), then the history picker (Last 12 Months, All History; stats/graphs-common G3); at compact width the title "Statistics" with the scope and history as its subtitle ("Japanese · Last 12 Months") and one toolbar menu with the same choices, the Search scope showing the navigation bar's search field. Choosing a deck never changes the current deck (R1353). Content: one scrolling grid of graph boxes, 3 columns on wide Mac windows, 2 at medium widths and iPad landscape, 1 on iPhone and narrow windows (R1359); each box is a system group box with Anki's title and subtitle (R1358), one row of the graph's controls, the chart and its table. Changing a graph's control re-bins without a core call (R1355); the range pickers are remembered per device (R1366); Backlog and Separate suspended/buried read and write their synced keys (stats/graphs-common G7); every other control follows stats/graph-presentation. On Mac a click on a clickable bar, cell or label opens Browse in the same window with the joined search (stats/browse-queries Q3) and hover shows its tooltip; on touch a first tap selects it and shows the tooltip with "Show in Browser" (R1417, R1418); coming back restores scope, controls, scroll position and selection (R1419). Loading: Stats opens at once on the last result for the scope, or on blank placeholders of the final size, and puts the new data in place without moving the layout (R1291); every open refreshes (R1294). Empty: a scope with no cards and no reviews: each box shows its empty state, `No Data`, with Card Counts keeping its table (stats/graph-presentation P16.5, R1361); the header stays usable. Error: a Search scope error shows its message (search/errors E7) in one line at the top of the content, under the search field at compact width, and the graphs shown stay (R1351); while a scope error shows, no item is clickable (stats/browse-queries Q2.3); a deck deleted while it is the scope (unknown_deck) shows "This deck no longer exists." in the same place; an unreadable row (stats/graphs-common G8.2) shows a content-unavailable view in place of the grid, saying Check Database can repair it, with a Check Database button once U128 lands. Live: after a change set, a rollover, a day-clock change or CollectionReplaced (G10) a visible Stats screen refreshes in place, about 500 ms after the last event, keeping every control and the scroll position (R1356); a hidden one refreshes when it appears. Overflow: the largest text sizes, a long deck name (middle truncation in the pop-up, full name as help text) and all graphs in one column scroll. Keyboard: Tab moves through the header controls, then each box's controls; ⌘F selects the Search scope and focuses its field; Return runs it; T opens Stats from Home and the deck page. VoiceOver: each box is a container named by its title; each chart has a summary and an audio graph (U226); an empty box reads stats/graph-presentation P18.1's "<title>. <scope>. No Data"; the header controls are labelled "Scope", "Deck", "Search" and "History". Identifiers stats.scope.deck, stats.scope.collection, stats.scope.search, stats.history.all (R1445). Core: stats/graphs-common G8 requests on the query lane, two per refresh (the graphs above the fold first, G8.3), the superseded one cancelled; the G7 preferences in the result; the G10 events; the scope text and the join of stats/browse-queries Q2 and Q3 in Swift; viewing writes nothing (G11, R1295).
- `stats.heatmapSettings`: The Heatmap settings section: Calendar mode, the Advanced disclosure with the history, forecast and date limits, the deleted-card and manual-reschedule exclusions and the excluded decks (R1339), first day of week, and the device-local display toggles. No colour theme: one native palette (R1315); the synced theme value is kept unchanged.

- `settings.root`: The settings sections and their preferences (native-interface-contract N5, N11.4). Mac: the separate Settings window (⌘,) with a sidebar of sections and a search field; iPad and iPhone: the Settings sidebar section or tab of the main window, sections as rows. Each section is a grouped form.
- `settings.sync`: Explicit Anki collection transfers and separate both-side media consent. Overflow renders media-consent; supplemental settings/anki-transfer routes media-progress, media-partial, media-complete and media-unknown cover Cancel, explicit Resume, long excluded names and unverified exclusions using the production controls with synthetic values and no server work.
- `settings.importExport`: Import packages and export decks or the collection.
- `settings.backups`: The Backups section (Mac: a Settings window sidebar section, plus File › Back Up Now and File › Restore from Backup…; iPad and iPhone: the Backups row of Settings). A grouped form: (1) "Back Up Now" with "Last backup: <date and time>" from the maintenance status (optimize-integrity M10), and the result "Created <file name> (<size>)" in the footer after a run; (2) "Restore from Backup…" and "Show in Finder" (Mac) or "Show in Files" (iPad, iPhone; Documents/Backups); (3) the limits with the Synced badge: "Back up every" N minutes (5–9999), "Daily backups", "Weekly backups", "Monthly backups" (0–9999 each), written only on change (package/backups B6.2). Each field shows the value B6.1 reads, even outside its range; an edit changes only the edited member and passes the other three read values to the B6.2 write unchanged. Footer "Backups don't include media files." and, once U162 attaches it, "Export Collection with Media…". The restore sheet (on the window it was opened from; the main window from the damaged-collection screen): title "Restore from Backup", a list newest first of date and time, size, and "Server copy" for a server copy; an unverified server copy is listed dimmed with "Can't be restored" and cannot be selected; the newest restorable entry is preselected; Cancel and Restore (disabled without a selection). The sheet stays open through the confirmation, the progress and a refusal, and closes on success. Restore asks first (confirmation-dialog): "Replace the current collection with the backup from <date>?", message "The current collection is backed up first. The restored collection stays on this device until you choose what to do with iCloud.", destructive Restore and Cancel. Loading: Back Up Now is a background job (package/backup-triggers T5): a non-modal activity in its row with Cancel while stopping is safe; only Back Up Now and Restore from Backup… are disabled meanwhile, and study and edits go on. The restore runs in the exclusive phase: its progress replaces the sheet's list, with Cancel while stopping is safe, and U153's gate disables mutating entry points app-wide. Error: a Back Up Now failure shows its cause in the section footer. A refused or failed restore shows one line in the sheet naming the cause and saying the current collection is unchanged: a backup that fails its check (the next-newest restorable entry is then preselected), a review session open, another operation running (named), the safety backup failing, not enough space. Empty: no backups yet; Restore from Backup… disabled with the footer "No backups yet". In Failed{Corrupt} Back Up Now and the limits are disabled and Restore stays. Success lands on the deck workspace with the iCloud publication choice that the pending iCloud contract defines.
- `settings.maintenance`: Check Database, Check Media and Empty Cards with their reports.
- `settings.diagnostics`: Diagnostic information and Copy Debug Info.
- `settings.integrations`: The AnkiConnect and Migaku servers, their state and access settings.
- `settings.migakuProfiles`: Routing profiles that map Migaku cards to decks and note types.
- `settings.recentlyReceived`: Notes the local servers created recently, with move actions.
